title: Why Kenji did the dishes
setting: Okaasan leaves a voice message for her daughter Yuki about Yuki's little brother Kenji, who was suddenly very helpful in the kitchen last night.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? okaasan da kedo. kinou no kenji, sugokatta no yo.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。昨日のケンジ、すごかったのよ。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。きのうのけんじ、すごかったのよ。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? It's Mum. You should have seen Kenji last night.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: gochisousama tte ittara, sugu osara arattoku yo tte. tanonde nai noni.
lines.ja: ごちそうさまって言ったら、すぐ「お皿洗っとくよ」って。頼んでないのに。
lines.kana: ごちそうさまっていったら、すぐ「おさらあらっとくよ」って。たのんでないのに。
lines.english: The moment we'd said thanks for the meal, he goes, 'I'll do the dishes.' I hadn't even asked!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: osara zenbu aratte, teeburu mo chanto fuite kureta no.
lines.ja: お皿全部洗って、テーブルもちゃんと拭いてくれたの。
lines.kana: おさらぜんぶあらって、テーブルもちゃんとふいてくれたの。
lines.english: He washed every single plate, and gave the table a proper wipe too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sorekara oyu wakasu kedo, nanka nomu? tte. ocha made motte kite kureta no.
lines.ja: それから「お湯沸かすけど、なんか飲む？」って。お茶まで持ってきてくれたの。
lines.kana: それから「おゆわかすけど、なんかのむ？」って。おちゃまでもってきてくれたの。
lines.english: Then he says, 'I'm putting the kettle on, want anything?' He even brought me a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mae wa oyu mo wakasenakatta noni ne. yatto otona ni natta naa tte omotta no.
lines.ja: 前はお湯も沸かせなかったのにね。やっと大人になったなあって思ったの。
lines.kana: まえはおゆもわかせなかったのにね。やっとおとなになったなあっておもったの。
lines.english: This from a boy who couldn't even boil water! I thought, he's finally grown up.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo ne, kesa gomi o dasou to shitara, naka ni wareta osara ga haitteta no.
lines.ja: でもね、今朝ゴミを出そうとしたら、中に割れたお皿が入ってたの。
lines.kana: でもね、けさごみをだそうとしたら、なかにわれたおさらがはいってたの。
lines.english: But this morning, when I went to take the rubbish out, there was a broken plate in it.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okaasan no daiji na osara. kinou, kenji ga watchatta no ne.
lines.ja: お母さんの大事なお皿。昨日、ケンジが割っちゃったのね。
lines.kana: おかあさんのだいじなおさら。きのう、けんじがわっちゃったのね。
lines.english: My favourite plate. Kenji must have broken it yesterday.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dakara kyuu ni, osara arattari, teeburu fuitari shite kureta no ne.
lines.ja: だから急に、お皿洗ったり、テーブル拭いたりしてくれたのね。
lines.kana: だからきゅうに、おさらあらったり、テーブルふいたりしてくれたのね。
lines.english: So that's why he was suddenly washing the dishes and wiping the table for me.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okottenai yo. kesa mo, mou oyu wakashite kureteta shi ne.
lines.ja: 怒ってないよ。今朝も、もうお湯沸かしてくれてたしね。
lines.kana: おこってないよ。けさも、もうおゆわかしてくれてたしね。
lines.english: I'm not angry. He even had the kettle on for me again this morning.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, okaasan ga shitteru koto, kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne. mou chotto tetsudatte hoshii kara.
lines.ja: でも、お母さんが知ってること、ケンジには内緒にしてね。もうちょっと手伝ってほしいから。
lines.kana: でも、おかあさんがしってること、けんじにはないしょにしてね。もうちょっとてつだってほしいから。
lines.english: But don't tell Kenji I know, OK? I want a bit more help out of him first.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa ne. yuki mo kondo kaette kitara, teeburu kurai fuite ne.
lines.ja: じゃあね。ユキも今度帰ってきたら、テーブルくらい拭いてね。
lines.kana: じゃあね。ゆきもこんどかえってきたら、テーブルくらいふいてね。
lines.english: Bye now. And next time you're home, you could at least wipe the table too.

choices.english: Kenji broke Mum's favourite plate, and she's angry and wants Yuki to have a word with him.
Kenji suddenly started helping because he wants something from Mum, and she wants Yuki to find out what.
Kenji was suddenly helpful in the kitchen because he'd broken Mum's favourite plate; she isn't angry, but wants Yuki to keep quiet so he keeps helping.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: without being asked, Kenji washed the dishes, wiped the table and put the kettle on, and in line 5 Mum thought he'd finally grown up. Lines 6-8: taking the rubbish out this morning, she found her favourite plate broken in it and worked out why he'd been so helpful (dakara kyuu ni ... shite kureta no ne). Lines 9-10: she isn't angry (okottenai yo), and asks Yuki not to tell Kenji she knows, because she wants a bit more help out of him. A is wrong because she says she isn't angry and wants it kept secret, not a talking-to. B is wrong because Mum already knows the reason; she asks Yuki to keep a secret, not to find anything out.

questions.english: You've just eaten a dinner Kenta cooked for you at his flat. He asks: "So? Are you full?" Thank him and offer to do the dishes.
questions.ja: どう？おなかいっぱいになった？
questions.kana: どう？おなかいっぱいになった？
questions.answer: Thank him and offer to wash up with osara (o) arau: un, gochisousama! osara wa watashi ga arau ne. Not osara o suru.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, gochisousama! osara wa watashi ga arau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ごちそうさま！お皿は私が洗うね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, thanks, that was lovely! I'll do the dishes.

modelAnswers.romaji: onaka ippai! tsukutte kureta kara, osara arattoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: おなかいっぱい！作ってくれたから、お皿洗っとくね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm stuffed! You cooked, so I'll wash up.

questions.explanation: Washing up is osara (o) arau, the same offer Kenji makes in line 2 (osara arattoku yo), and in line 3 he does it (osara zenbu aratte). English 'do the dishes' tempts osara o suru, but suru doesn't go with osara. If you want suru, put it on the chore noun instead: sara-arai suru or araimono suru (araimono shitoku ne). Saying osara wa watashi ga arau ne ('the dishes, I'll do') makes it an offer.

questions.english: Mum quotes what Kenji asked her after he'd washed up. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは、お母さんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんは、おかあさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa, okaasan ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: I'm simmering some water, want anything?
I'm putting the kettle on, want anything?
I'm boiling up some water, want anything?

questions.explanation: Line 4: Mum quotes Kenji, oyu wakasu kedo, nanka nomu?, and in line 9 he had the water on again this morning (oyu wakashite kureteta). Water is heated with wakasu, and it's already called oyu (hot water) before it boils. A uses niru, where English 'boil' often points, but niru is simmering food (vegetables, fish) in a broth, never water on its own. C uses yuderu, which is boiling food in water (eggs, pasta, noodles): you yuderu the egg, not the water. Line 5 uses the same verb as the right answer: oyu mo wakasenakatta, 'couldn't even boil water'.

questions.english: You're cooking dinner at your parents' place, and it's nearly ready. Your mum comes in and asks: "Want me to help with anything?" Ask her to give the table a wipe.
questions.answer: Ask for a wipe with teeburu (o) fuku as a casual request: jaa, teeburu fuite kureru? A table gets wiped with a cloth (fuku), not washed (arau).

modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、テーブル拭いてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Then could you give the table a wipe?

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. mou sugu dekiru kara, teeburu fuitoite.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。もうすぐできるから、テーブル拭いといて。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. It's nearly ready, so could you wipe the table?

questions.explanation: Wiping with a cloth is fuku: Kenji gave the table a wipe (teeburu mo chanto fuite kureta, line 3; teeburu fuitari, line 8), and Mum's parting shot in line 11, teeburu kurai fuite ne, is the same request you're making. Don't say teeburu o arau: arau is washing with water, which is what happened to the dishes in the same breath (osara zenbu aratte, teeburu mo ... fuite). And souji suru is for cleaning a room or the whole house; a table just gets a wipe. -te kureru? or -toite (fuite oite, 'get it done') turns it into a casual request.

newWords.english: break, get broken (wareta osara = a broken plate)
at least, even just (teeburu kurai = at least the table)
